title: Mass. to be 4th state to roll out EBT chip cards to curb fraud
author: Morgan Rousseau
bullets: Massachusetts to distribute chip-enabled EBT cards statewide to protect SNAP and public assistance benefits from fraud.
Nearly 1 million residents use EBT cards at 5,500 retailers; the state distributes $2.6 billion in SNAP benefits annually.
Retailers are updating payment systems for new cards; some stores may still require swiping until systems are ready.

title: Boston is now offering ‘pet certificates’ for couples who wed at City Hall
author: Morgan Rousseau
bullets: Boston City Hall now offers 'pet certificates' for couples who marry there, recognizing family pets in the marriage ceremony.
Mayor Michelle Wu announced the initiative, highlighting the shared commitment and love pets bring to households.
The 'Family Companion Status Record' includes the City of Boston seal and declares the pet an honored household member.

title: Kevin Nealon discusses Conan, Dunkin’, SNL and more ahead of local shows
author: Lauren Daley
bullets: Kevin Nealon discusses his comedic evolution, including his Twitter presence and the use of social media.
Nealon shares details about his upcoming shows in Boston and Portsmouth, New Hampshire.
His new comedy special 'Loose in the Crotch' is streaming on YouTube, exploring themes of aging and parenting.

title: Red Sox’ Willson Contreras leaves game after scary HBP vs. Dodgers
author: Kaley Brown
bullets: Red Sox' Willson Contreras hit by a 95 MPH fastball from Dodgers' Will Klein, left the game for precaution.
Contreras walked to first base after being hit, but was substituted defensively the next inning by Nick Sogard.
Manager Chad Tracy reports Contreras's initial tests are fine; concussion concerns remain pending further evaluation.

title: After Patriots coaching stint, DeAndre Hopkins joins Georgia Tech staff
author: Kaley Brown
bullets: DeAndre Hopkins, 34, joins Georgia Tech as assistant wide receivers coach after brief coaching role with New England Patriots.
Georgia Tech head coach David Key highlights Hopkins's offensive knowledge and leadership as key assets to the team.
Hopkins's new role follows training camp appearance, with no formal NFL retirement announced; Georgia Tech hosts Boston College Oct. 24.

title: Could Efton Chism and Kyle Williams both make the Patriots 53-man roster?
author: Colin McCarthy
bullets: Efton Chism and Kyle Williams are competing for spots on the Patriots' 53-man roster.
Chism, an undrafted rookie, is impressing in camp but is less known than his competitor Williams.
Williams, though lower on the depth chart, is showing enough talent to potentially secure a roster spot.

title: Reports: OF George Springer interested in trade to Red Sox, team eyeing INF Xavier Edwards
author: Kaley Brown
bullets: George Springer is open to being traded from the Blue Jays to the Red Sox, pending team circumstances.
The Red Sox are interested in Miami Marlins' infielder Xavier Edwards as a potential solution for their infield needs.
Springer, 36, has a strong record at Fenway Park, but is having a below-average season with a .234 batting average.

title: 5 must-watch movies & TV shows streaming right now
author: Kevin Slane
bullets: 'The Devil Wears Prada 2', featuring Meryl Streep and Anne Hathaway, is now streaming on Hulu.
'The Drama', a dark comedy set in Boston with Zendaya and Robert Pattinson, is available on HBO Max.
New TV show 'Furious' Season 1, starring Emmy Rossum, is streaming on Hulu.

title: Here’s how home, away broadcasts reacted to Jarren Duran’s on-field flare-up
author: Kaley Brown
bullets: Jarren Duran caused controversy by reacting angrily during the Red Sox's game against the Athletics, targeting teammate Willson Contreras.
Both NESN and WEEI broadcasts were critical of Duran's actions, with commentators expressing confusion and disapproval at his outburst.
Duran's frustration was reportedly aimed at third base coach Chad Epperson, and Red Sox may trade him before the MLB deadline.

title: Drake Maye on building chemistry with A.J. Brown: ‘I am not going to shy away from him.’
author: Khari A. Thompson
bullets: Drake Maye and A.J. Brown are developing chemistry during the New England Patriots training camp, finding success in practice routines.
Maye's aggressive approach in targeting Brown in drills has improved their on-field connection, with repeated completions during team exercises.
Frequent communication off the field between Maye and Brown enhances their understanding and ability to execute plays effectively.
